terra.problem: Papa claims he has sent people to a store. That adds an unsupported event outside his established world.
The text does not say where the flocks stay. Marking it as a guess does not establish that event.
The text does not say anyone had to count the donkeys or that it was a long day.
The explanation is a flat repetition of the count, without much of Papa's personality.
The claim that the brothers sold Joseph comes from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The floor joke doesn't make sense: their faces are already to the ground.
The line about gifts later in the story gives away a future detail and states an outside-passage fact without a reference.
Joseph recognizes his brothers, but the text does not say he already knows where they have come from.
The text does not say whether anyone offered them a seat or that Joseph gave them a hard stare.
Saying the brothers are stuck until the youngest arrives overlooks Joseph's later condition allowing the others to leave while one stays in custody.
The explanation is a generic repetition of the answer and verse, with little of Papa's voice.
The claim that this is years later relies on facts outside the passage and needs references.
Judah being Jacob's son is a fact from outside this passage and needs a reference.
The passage does not establish that Levi says nothing during the scene.
The text says Joseph understood them, but does not say they talked freely or that he heard every word.
The text does not say the brothers thought their conversation was private or that Joseph heard all of it.
Calling it a tough moment for the whole group states their feelings without marking them as Papa's inference.
The text does not establish that nobody said a word about the returned silver.
The claim that a robe would not fit in a sack's mouth is unsupported, and the joke does not clearly make sense.
The text does not say the reported promise is what the brothers hold onto when they speak to Jacob.
Nobody's moving anywhere is broader than the text supports and makes a claim about what happens next.
The calculator joke puts a modern object into the Bible scene, and the passage does not place the scene in a tent.
The explanation states Reuben's reason for the offer as fact, though the text does not give it.
At least not yet hints at what happens next in a story that is not over.
